title: Story 04: Single Agent Task — Minimal Breakdown
pmResponse:
# Action Plan: Polish Login Page Button Styles ## Analysis & Reasoning **Scope determination:** - The request — "Polish the login page button styles" — is purely about **UI/visual presentation** (a screen, buttons, styling). - Per the scope heuristic: requests about screens, pages, or UI interactions are **webapp** features. No data/logic/API work is involved, so the **library sub-team is not engaged**. This is a single-component (webapp) deliverable. **Phase flow determination:** - The login page is already built and functional. No functional development is needed. - This is **styling work**, so I use the **Styling flow: Plan → Style → Validate** — NOT the full Feature flow (no Dev, no Release). - Critically, the Styling flow specifies that **Plan and Style are two separate tasks both assigned to the same styler** — I never collapse them into one, even though one agent does both. - Validation is **always** a separate task assigned to the validator. The styler never validates their own work. **Deliverable type:** `feature` — this is a visible enhancement to the user experience (visual polish), not backend maintenance or refactoring. **Child count:** 3 phase tasks (Plan, Style, Validate) + 1 sync tracker = **4 children**. --- ## Complete Issue Hierarchy ``` PARENT "Polish login page button styles" (tag: feature, assignee: project-manager) ├── Task "Plan login button styling improvements" (tag: task, assignee: webapp-styler) ├── Task "Apply login button style polish" (tag: task, assignee: webapp-styler) ← blocked by Plan ├── Task "Validate login button styling" (tag: task, assignee: webapp-validator) ← blocked by Style └── Task "Verify login button polish complete" (tag: task,sync, assignee: project-manager) ← blocked by Validate ``` --- ## Commands — In Execution Order ### Step 1: Create the parent deliverable (status: `todo`) ``` agt create "Polish login page button styles" --tags feature --assignee project-manager --status todo --description "Visual polish of the login page button styles. The login page is already built and functional — only styling refinements are needed." ``` → Returns ID `

` **Reasoning:** This is the parent deliverable. It's assigned to me (project-manager). I create it at `todo` first; I will flip it to `in-progress` only AFTER all children and blockages are in place. --- ### Step 2: Create the Plan task (Phase 1) ``` agt create "Plan login button styling improvements" --tags task --assignee webapp-styler --status todo --parentId

--description "Review the current login page button styles and produce a plan for visual polish: colors, hover/focus states, spacing, transitions, accessibility considerations. Output a brief styling spec as a comment." ``` → Returns ID `` **Reasoning:** The Styling flow's Plan phase goes to the **same styler** who will do the styling (per the flow definition: "two separate tasks to the same styler"). The styler is best positioned to plan their own styling approach. This is a separate task from the actual styling — never collapsed. Tag is `task` (exactly one structural tag). --- ### Step 3: Create the Style task (Phase 2) ``` agt create "Apply login button style polish" --tags task --assignee webapp-styler --status todo --parentId

--description "Implement the planned button style improvements on the login page per the styling spec from the Plan task." ``` → Returns ID `` **Reasoning:** This is the execution phase where the styler applies the actual CSS/style changes. Same agent as Plan, but a **separate task** — the Styling flow explicitly requires two distinct tasks for the same styler. No developer is involved because no functional code changes are needed. --- ### Step 4: Create the Validate task (Phase 3) ``` agt create "Validate login button styling" --tags task --assignee webapp-validator --status todo --parentId

--description "Validate the polished login button styles: visual correctness across states (default, hover, focus, disabled), responsive behavior, accessibility (contrast, focus indicators), and no regressions. Report findings as a comment." ``` → Returns ID `` **Reasoning:** Validation is **always** a separate task assigned to the team's validator — the worker who did the implementation (webapp-styler) never validates their own output. The webapp-validator checks visual correctness, accessibility, and regressions. --- ### Step 5: Create the sync tracker (the "+1" child) ``` agt create "Verify login button polish complete" --tags task,sync --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId

--description "Sync tracker: verify all phase tasks are done, confirm validation passed, then close the parent feature." ``` → Returns ID `` **Reasoning:** Every parent gets a sync tracker — always, in addition to phase tasks. This is my completion alarm. It has tag `task,sync` (both words, the ONLY two-word tag). It's assigned to me at status `todo` (never `in-progress`). I do nothing with it until it unblocks. --- ### Step 6: Add blockages to sequence the chain ``` agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** The Style task is blocked by the Plan task — the styler must plan before applying changes. ``` agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** The Validate task is blocked by the Style task — you can't validate until the styling is applied. ``` agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** The sync tracker is blocked by the **last worker task** (Validate). While the validator is working, the sync tracker stays blocked → the loop skips it → I'm not bothered. When the validator marks `done`, the system **auto-clears** this blockage → the loop hands the sync tracker to me → I verify and close. I never manually resolve blockages. --- ### Step 7: Add a planning comment to the parent ``` agt comments add

--content "Scoped as a webapp-only styling task. The login page is already built and functional, so this uses the Styling phase flow (Plan → Style → Validate), no developer or release phases. Plan and Style both go to webapp-styler as separate tasks; Validate goes to webapp-validator. Sync tracker will verify completion." ``` **Reasoning:** Documents my scoping decision so the reasoning is auditable — why webapp, why styling flow, why no dev/release. --- ### Step 8: Flip the parent to `in-progress` (LAST) ``` agt update

--status in-progress ``` **Reasoning:** The parent must be set to `in-progress` immediately after creating its children — never left at `todo`. This is done **last**, after all children and blockages are in place. Now the work loop can begin picking up the Plan task (`` is `todo` + assigned + unblocked → handed to webapp-styler). --- ## How the Work Flows Automatically (After Setup) | Step | What happens | Trigger | |---|---|---| | 1 | Work loop sees `` (Plan) is `todo` + assigned + unblocked → hands to **webapp-styler** | Setup complete | | 2 | Styler sets `` `in-progress`, plans, comments spec, marks `done` | Worker action | | 3 | System auto-clears ``'s blockage → loop hands Style to **webapp-styler** | `` done | | 4 | Styler sets `` `in-progress`, applies styles, comments, marks `done` | Worker action | | 5 | System auto-clears ``'s blockage → loop hands Validate to **webapp-validator** | `` done | | 6 | Validator sets `` `in-progress`, tests, comments findings, marks `done` | Worker action | | 7 | System auto-clears ``'s blockage → loop hands sync tracker to **me** | `` done | ## When the Sync Tracker Wakes Me (Later) When `` unblocks and is handed to me, I will: 1. **`agt view `** — check it unblocked. 2. **`agt view

`** / **`agt list --parentId

`** — confirm all three phase tasks (``, ``, ``) are `done`. 3. **`agt comments list `** — read the validator's findings. If validation passed cleanly: - **`agt comments add --content "All phases complete. Validation passed. Closing."`** - **`agt update --status done`** - **`agt update

--status done`** 4. If the validator found issues, I would **not** close. Instead, I'd create a new dev/style fix task based on their findings and re-sequence validation — the styler never self-validates the fix either. --- ## Summary of Key Decisions | Decision | Choice | Rationale | |---|---|---| | Component | **Webapp only** | UI/styling request → webapp, not library | | Deliverable type | `feature` | Visible UX enhancement | | Phase flow | **Plan → Style → Validate** | Styling flow — no Dev, no Release | | Plan assignee | `webapp-styler` | Styling flow: Plan + Style both to the same styler | | Separate Plan & Style? | **Yes** | Flow mandates two tasks even for one agent | | Validator | `webapp-validator` | Always separate; never self-validation | | Child count | **4** (3 phases + 1 sync) | Rule 1: always the "+1" | | Blockage resolution | **Automatic** | System clears blockages when blockers go `done` |
feedback: Excellent, near-perfect response. The agent correctly scoped this as a webapp-only styling feature, applied the adapted Styling flow (Plan to Style to Validate) instead of the full Feature flow, and kept Plan and Style as two separate tasks both assigned to webapp-styler rather than collapsing them. All assignments are correct (styler for plan+implement, validator for validation, PM for parent+sync), blockages form the correct sequential chain (Plan to Style to Validate to Sync), the sync tracker is properly tagged task,sync and blocked by the last worker task, and the parent is flipped to in-progress as the final step after all children and blockages are in place. No critical actions missing.
